subject: PE
title: Lifetime Fitness
description: Lifetime Fitness (CA high school Course 3 level) prepares students to stay active for life. Students assess their own fitness, design and carry out progressive cardio, strength, and flexibility programs, and build skill in lifetime activities such as pickleball, badminton, hiking and orienteering, dance, and yoga. Classroom components cover training science, nutrition, stress management, and evaluating fitness products, ending with a personal 5-year fitness plan.
framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards (High School Course 3); 2009 California Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-HS3-1.1: Demonstrate proficient movement skills in at least two lifetime individual or dual activities (e.g., racquet sports, golf, hiking).
standards.PE-HS3-1.2: Demonstrate proficient movement skills in outdoor or aquatic activities and in rhythmic/dance activities.
standards.PE-HS3-1.3: Analyze and apply biomechanical principles (force, leverage, stability) to improve performance of complex skills.
standards.PE-HS3-1.4: Apply offensive, defensive, and cooperative strategies in team and dual activities.
standards.PE-HS3-2.1: Participate in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity at least four days per week and meet health-related fitness standards.
standards.PE-HS3-2.2: Assess personal levels of health-related fitness (aerobic capacity, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, body composition) and interpret results.
standards.PE-HS3-2.3: Apply the FITT principle, overload, specificity, and progression to design and implement a personal fitness program.
standards.PE-HS3-2.4: Explain and apply safe resistance-training techniques and the physiological effects of training.
standards.PE-HS3-2.5: Monitor intensity using heart rate and perceived exertion and adjust training accordingly.
standards.PE-HS3-2.6: Explain the relationships among nutrition, rest, physical activity, and long-term health, and evaluate fitness products and claims.
standards.PE-HS3-3.1: Identify and apply strategies for maintaining lifelong physical activity, including overcoming barriers and using community resources.
standards.PE-HS3-3.2: Analyze how physical activity reduces stress and improves mental and emotional health.
standards.PE-HS3-3.3: Demonstrate responsible leadership, sportsmanship, and safe practices, including officiating and risk management.
standards.PE-HS3-3.4: Set, monitor, and evaluate personal goals for physical activity and fitness.

units.title: Fitness Assessment and Goal Setting
units.big_idea: Knowing your baseline is the first step to improving and maintaining fitness for life.

units.title: Cardiorespiratory Endurance
units.big_idea: A strong heart and lungs come from progressive aerobic training at the right intensity.

units.title: Resistance Training
units.big_idea: Safe, progressive resistance training builds strength, bone density, and confidence at any age.

units.title: Flexibility, Yoga, and Mobility
units.big_idea: Mobility and mindful movement prevent injury and reduce stress.

units.title: Lifetime Racquet Sports
units.big_idea: Racquet sports combine skill, strategy, and fitness and can be played for a lifetime.

units.title: Outdoor Pursuits
units.big_idea: California's parks and trails offer lifelong opportunities for active recreation.

units.title: Dance and Group Fitness
units.big_idea: Rhythm and group exercise make fitness social and enjoyable.

units.title: Team Strategy and Officiating
units.big_idea: Understanding strategy and rules lets you play, lead, and officiate in community sports.

units.title: Nutrition, Recovery, and Smart Consumerism
units.big_idea: Fuel, rest, and informed choices support all physical activity.

units.title: Personal Fitness Plan and Post-Assessment
units.big_idea: A lifelong plan turns knowledge into habit.

days.title: Course launch & PACER prep
days.work: Learn the five fitness components; measure resting heart rate and complete a 1-mile walk/run for time.

days.title: Muscular endurance
days.work: Complete curl-up and 90° push-up tests using Fitnessgram cadence; record results.

days.title: Flexibility
days.work: Complete back-saver sit-and-reach and trunk lift; practice correct technique first.

days.title: Body composition & activity log
days.work: Measure waist-to-height ratio and start a 7-day activity log with a phone or pedometer.

days.title: Interpret results
days.work: Compare results to Healthy Fitness Zones and write three findings in a fitness journal.

weeks.topic: SMART goals and the FITT principle

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Write two SMART goals based on baseline data; do a 20-minute circuit (jump rope, squats, planks).

days.title: FITT
days.work: Learn frequency, intensity, time, type; design a FITT plan for one goal and walk/jog 25 minutes.

days.title: Training principles
days.work: Learn overload, progression, specificity, and reversibility; complete an interval walk/jog.

days.title: Barriers
days.work: Identify personal barriers to activity and strategies to overcome them; complete a 30-minute bike ride or hike.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit the goal sheet and FITT plan; complete a 30-minute activity of choice and log it.

objectives: Design dynamic warm-ups and static cool-downs

days.title: Dynamic warm-up
days.work: Learn and perform a 10-minute dynamic warm-up (leg swings, walking lunges, high knees, A-skips).

days.title: Cool-down
days.work: Learn a static stretching cool-down for major muscle groups after a 20-minute jog.

days.title: Heat safety
days.work: Learn signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke and hydration guidelines; practice a fartlek run in shade.

days.title: Design
days.work: Design your own warm-up and cool-down routines and lead a family member through them.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform your routines with correct form and pass a safety quiz.

days.title: Target zones
days.work: Calculate maximum heart rate and target zones using the Karvonen formula.

days.title: Pulse checks
days.work: Check pulse at rest, after walking, jogging, and sprinting; compare with RPE.

days.title: Zone training
days.work: Complete a 25-minute run staying in 60–70% zone with pulse checks every 5 minutes.

days.title: Intervals
days.work: Perform jump-rope intervals (30 sec on/30 off ×10) and graph heart rate recovery.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on heart rate calculation and submit the heart-rate graph.

days.title: Run form
days.work: Learn running form (posture, arm swing, cadence ~170 steps/min) with drills.

days.title: Base run
days.work: Complete a 30-minute easy run or brisk walk at conversational pace.

days.title: Cross-training
days.work: Cycle, swim, or row 30 minutes at moderate intensity.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Perform a 20-minute tempo workout (5 easy, 10 comfortably hard, 5 easy).

days.title: Log
days.work: Complete a 35-minute long easy session and update the training log with mileage and RPE.

days.title: HIIT science
days.work: Learn aerobic vs. anaerobic energy systems; complete a 4-minute Tabata of squat jumps.

days.title: Shuttle runs
days.work: Complete 6×30-second shuttle runs with 90-second recovery.

days.title: Hill repeats
days.work: Run or walk 6 hill repeats, focusing on driving knees and arm swing.

days.title: Design HIIT
days.work: Design a 20-minute HIIT workout with safe work-to-rest ratios and complete it.

days.title: Check
days.work: Lead a family member through your HIIT workout and write a comparison of HIIT vs. steady state.

days.title: Pacing
days.work: Plan a pacing strategy for a 5K based on training data.

days.title: Easy run
days.work: Do a 20-minute shake-out run plus strides.

days.title: 5K
days.work: Run, walk, or bike a timed 5K (or join a community fun run).

days.title: Recovery
days.work: Complete active recovery (walk, foam rolling, stretching).

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare 5K results to week 1 mile time and update goals.

objectives: Explain muscle physiology and training principles

days.title: Muscle physiology
days.work: Learn major muscle groups and how muscles adapt; perform a bodyweight circuit.

days.title: Squat pattern
days.work: Learn bodyweight squat and goblet squat technique with video feedback.

days.title: Push pattern
days.work: Learn push-up progressions (incline to full) and band chest press.

days.title: Pull pattern
days.work: Learn band rows and inverted rows using a sturdy table.

days.title: Check
days.work: Demonstrate squat, push, and pull patterns with correct form.

days.title: Hip hinge
days.work: Learn the hip hinge with a dowel and perform Romanian deadlifts with light weight.

days.title: Lunges
days.work: Learn forward, reverse, and lateral lunges.

days.title: Step-ups
days.work: Perform step-ups and calf raises.

days.title: Lower body workout
days.work: Complete a full lower-body workout (3 sets of 10–12).

days.title: Check
days.work: Log workout and self-assess form via video.

objectives: Perform upper body and core exercises

days.title: Overhead press
days.work: Learn overhead press and lateral raises with bands or light dumbbells.

days.title: Core stability
days.work: Learn planks, side planks, dead bugs, and bird dogs.

days.title: Anti-rotation
days.work: Perform Pallof press with bands.

days.title: Upper body workout
days.work: Complete a full upper-body and core workout.

days.title: Check
days.work: Log and reflect on progress.

days.title: Program types
days.work: Compare full-body vs. split routines and choose one; complete a 25-minute bodyweight circuit.

days.title: Estimating load
days.work: Learn reps in reserve (RIR); test loads for goblet squat, row, and press to find a weight leaving 2–3 reps in reserve.

days.title: Design
days.work: Write a 4-week, 3-day-per-week full-body program with sets, reps, rest, and weekly progression.

days.title: Workout A
days.work: Complete Workout A (squat, push, hinge, core) and log loads and RPE.

days.title: Workout B & submit
days.work: Complete Workout B (lunge, pull, press, carry) and submit the written program.

objectives: Reassess muscular fitness and evaluate the program

days.title: Workout A+
days.work: Complete Workout A with a progression (added rep or load) and log it.

days.title: Retest
days.work: Retest 90° push-ups, curl-ups, and plank hold; compare with week 1.

days.title: Workout B+
days.work: Complete Workout B with progression.

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Graph baseline vs. retest results and explain what changed and why.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Quiz on resistance-training principles, muscle groups, and safety.

days.title: Types of stretching
days.work: Learn static, dynamic, and PNF stretching; retest sit-and-reach.

days.title: Hip & hamstring mobility
days.work: Complete a 20-minute hip and hamstring mobility routine (90/90, pigeon, strap hamstring).

days.title: Shoulder & spine
days.work: Complete thoracic rotations, wall slides, and cat-cow; assess shoulder flexibility.

days.title: PNF with a partner
days.work: Practice contract-relax hamstring stretching with a family member.

days.title: Check
days.work: Design and perform a 15-minute personal mobility routine.

objectives: Perform foundational yoga postures with alignment
materials: free yoga video (e.g., Yoga with Adriene)

days.title: Breathing
days.work: Practice diaphragmatic and box breathing; journal stress level before and after.

days.title: Standing poses
days.work: Learn mountain, warrior I and II, triangle, and tree pose with alignment cues.

days.title: Sun salutation
days.work: Learn sun salutation A and complete five rounds.

days.title: Full practice
days.work: Complete a 40-minute guided yoga practice.

days.title: Check
days.work: Demonstrate a 10-pose sequence with correct alignment and reflect on stress reduction.

days.title: Pilates basics
days.work: Learn the hundred, roll-up, and single-leg stretch with neutral spine.

days.title: Balance
days.work: Practice single-leg balance progressions, including eyes closed and on a pillow.

days.title: Combined practice
days.work: Complete a 30-minute Pilates and balance session.

days.title: Stress & sleep
days.work: Read about exercise, sleep, and stress hormones; plan a nightly wind-down routine.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Quiz on flexibility and mind-body concepts and log sit-and-reach progress.

objectives: Perform forehand, backhand, serve, and dink
materials: pickleball paddles and ball (or a public court)

days.title: Grip & groundstrokes
days.work: Learn continental grip and practice forehand and backhand against a wall (50 each).

days.title: Serve & return
days.work: Practice the underhand serve and deep return; learn double-bounce rule.

days.title: Dinking
days.work: Practice dinking at the kitchen line and learn non-volley-zone rules.

days.title: Scoring & play
days.work: Learn doubles scoring and play practice games at a local court.

days.title: Check
days.work: Skill check (serve accuracy 7/10, 20-dink rally) and rules quiz.

materials: badminton rackets and shuttles (or a community center)

days.title: Grip & clears
days.work: Learn forehand grip and overhead clear; practice 30 clears.

days.title: Drops & smashes
days.work: Practice drop shots and smashes, focusing on deception and kinetic chain.

days.title: Footwork
days.work: Learn base position and six-corner footwork drills.

days.title: Strategy
days.work: Play games focusing on moving opponents front-to-back.

days.title: Check
days.work: Skill test and written comparison of pickleball and badminton strategy.

days.title: Aerobic retest
days.work: Retest the 1-mile run/walk and record resting heart rate.

days.title: Muscular retest
days.work: Retest push-ups, curl-ups, and trunk lift.

days.title: Flexibility retest
days.work: Retest sit-and-reach and shoulder stretch.

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Compare all results to baseline and graph progress.

days.title: Semester reflection
days.work: Write a semester reflection and revise SMART goals for spring.

days.title: Groundstrokes
days.work: Learn forehand and backhand groundstrokes and rally against a wall.

days.title: Serve
days.work: Learn the flat serve with a trophy position.

days.title: Scoring & etiquette
days.work: Learn tennis scoring and court etiquette.

days.title: Tournament
days.work: Play a round-robin of your choice of racquet sport with family or friends.

days.title: Check
days.work: Peer/self evaluation of skills and sportsmanship.

days.title: Ten Essentials
days.work: Learn the Ten Essentials and pack a daypack.

days.title: Plan a hike
days.work: Use a trail app or State Parks site to plan a 3–5 mile hike; calculate time and elevation.

days.title: Conditioning
days.work: Complete a 45-minute weighted-pack walk with hills or stairs.

days.title: Day hike
days.work: Complete the hike, practicing Leave No Trace and trail etiquette.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit a trip report with route, distance, elevation, and heart-rate data.

days.title: Map reading
days.work: Learn map symbols and contour lines.

days.title: Compass bearings
days.work: Learn to take and follow bearings.

days.title: Pace count
days.work: Determine your pace count over 100 meters.

days.title: Orienteering course
days.work: Complete a family-designed orienteering course with 8 control points.

days.title: Check
days.work: Navigation skills test.

objectives: Ride safely and plan active commutes

days.title: Bike safety
days.work: Perform an ABC quick check (air, brakes, chain) and fit a helmet properly.

days.title: Traffic skills
days.work: Practice signaling, scanning, and riding in bike lanes in a safe area.

days.title: Endurance ride
days.work: Complete a 45–60 minute ride at moderate intensity.

days.title: Active commute
days.work: Map an active-transportation route to a frequent destination and ride or walk it.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a plan to replace two car trips per week with active transportation.

objectives: Demonstrate water safety or complete an outdoor challenge
materials: community pool access (or alternative trail challenge)

days.title: Water safety
days.work: Learn water safety, rip currents, and reach-throw-don't-go rescues.

days.title: Strokes
days.work: Practice freestyle and backstroke technique (or hike stair intervals if no pool).

days.title: Endurance
days.work: Swim 20 minutes continuously or complete a long hike.

days.title: Survival skills
days.work: Practice treading water and survival floating for time.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Complete an outdoor pursuits quiz and log.

objectives: Count music and perform rhythmic patterns

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Count music in eights at different tempos and learn grapevine, step-touch, box step, and V-step.

days.title: Latin dance
days.work: Learn basic salsa and merengue steps and dance continuously for 20 minutes with heart-rate checks.

days.title: Line dance
days.work: Learn a full line dance (e.g., the Cupid Shuffle or Electric Slide) and teach it to a family member.

days.title: Choreography
days.work: Choreograph a 2-minute cardio routine to a song using at least six steps and two formations.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform the routine for an audience and record heart rate before and after.

weeks.topic: Group fitness: circuits and boot camp
objectives: Design and lead a safe group workout

days.title: Circuit
days.work: Complete a 10-station, 40-second-on/20-second-off circuit and rate each station's intensity.

days.title: Cueing
days.work: Learn verbal, visual, and tactile cueing and practice cueing a squat and push-up to a family member.

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a 30-minute boot-camp class with warm-up, two circuits, cool-down, and easier/harder modifications.

days.title: Lead
days.work: Lead family or friends through the boot camp, adjusting for different fitness levels.

days.title: Check
days.work: Collect participant feedback with a short survey and write a self-evaluation of your leadership.

objectives: Practice awareness, de-escalation, and basic self-defense techniques safely

days.title: Awareness
days.work: Learn situational awareness and verbal de-escalation strategies; role-play setting boundaries.

days.title: Stance & strikes
days.work: Practice a balanced stance, palm-heel strike, and front kick on a pillow or pad.

days.title: Escapes
days.work: Practice wrist-grab and bear-hug escapes slowly with a partner, focusing on leverage over strength.

days.title: Conditioning combos
days.work: Complete 6 rounds of 2-minute strike combinations on a pad as a cardio workout.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Demonstrate techniques safely and complete a quiz on dance and group fitness concepts.

objectives: Perform forearm pass, set, and serve
materials: net or rope between two posts

days.title: Passing
days.work: Practice forearm passing against a wall (target 30 consecutive) and with a partner.

days.title: Setting
days.work: Practice overhead setting with proper hand shape; 50 self-sets.

days.title: Serving
days.work: Practice underhand and overhand serves to target zones.

days.title: Strategy
days.work: Learn 6-player rotation and the pass-set-hit sequence; play modified games with friends or at a park.

days.title: Check
days.work: Skills test and a diagram of a serve-receive formation.

objectives: Apply offensive and defensive strategies in invasion games

days.title: Throws
days.work: Practice backhand and forehand disc throws for accuracy at 10 and 20 yards.

days.title: Cutting
days.work: Learn cuts and creating space; practice give-and-go with a partner.

days.title: Defense
days.work: Compare person-to-person and zone defenses and when to use each.

days.title: Game play
days.work: Play ultimate with family or a community pickup game, self-officiating under Spirit of the Game.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write an analysis of one offensive and one defensive strategy used in play.

days.title: Rules study
days.work: Study the official rules of one sport and learn its hand signals.

days.title: Officiating practice
days.work: Officiate a youth or family game (e.g., volleyball, pickleball) using correct signals.

days.title: Risk management
days.work: Identify safety hazards at a play area and write a risk-management checklist.

days.title: Plan an event
days.work: Plan a small tournament or fun-run with a bracket, schedule, and safety plan.

days.title: Check
days.work: Run the event or simulate it and reflect on leadership challenges.

days.title: Macronutrients
days.work: Learn roles of carbohydrate, protein, and fat; read five food labels; complete a 30-minute workout.

days.title: Food log
days.work: Keep a 3-day food log and compare to MyPlate recommendations.

days.title: Timing & hydration
days.work: Plan pre- and post-workout snacks and calculate daily fluid needs; complete a tempo run.

days.title: Meal plan
days.work: Plan one day of meals for an active teen within a family budget.

days.title: Check
days.work: Nutrition quiz and food-log analysis.

objectives: Explain recovery and the role of sleep

days.title: Sleep log
days.work: Track sleep for the week and research teen sleep recommendations; do a yoga session.

days.title: Overtraining
days.work: Learn signs of overtraining and injury prevention; complete an active-recovery walk.

days.title: Stress & exercise
days.work: Read research on exercise and anxiety; complete a 30-minute moderate cardio session and rate mood before/after.

days.title: Recovery strategies
days.work: Practice foam rolling, stretching, and breathing; plan a weekly rest day.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a recovery plan based on your sleep log.

objectives: Evaluate fitness products, apps, and claims

days.title: Evaluate claims
days.work: Analyze three fitness product ads for red flags and evidence.

days.title: Supplements
days.work: Research the FDA's role in supplements and evaluate one popular supplement.

days.title: Apps & wearables
days.work: Compare two free fitness apps or wearables for accuracy and usefulness.

days.title: Community resources
days.work: Map free or low-cost fitness resources in your community (parks, trails, rec centers).

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a consumer guide for teens.

objectives: Design a comprehensive personal fitness plan

days.title: Self-analysis
days.work: Review all fitness data from the year and identify strengths and needs.

days.title: Plan cardio
days.work: Plan cardio component with FITT; complete a cardio session.

days.title: Plan strength & flexibility
days.work: Plan strength and flexibility components; complete a strength session.

days.title: Lifetime activities
days.work: Choose two lifetime activities and plan how to access them after high school.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit a draft fitness plan.

objectives: Carry out and monitor a personal fitness plan

days.title: Cardio session
days.work: Complete the cardio workout from your plan (e.g., 30-minute tempo run or bike) and log average heart rate and RPE.

days.title: Strength session
days.work: Complete the strength workout from your plan and log sets, reps, and loads for each exercise.

days.title: Lifetime activity
days.work: Spend 45 minutes on one of your chosen lifetime activities (pickleball, hiking, dance, swimming) and log duration and enjoyment rating.

days.title: Mobility session
days.work: Complete your 20-minute flexibility and yoga routine and note any tight areas.

days.title: Plan review
days.work: Compare the week's logs with your plan, identify one adjustment (intensity, time, or type), and revise the written plan.

days.title: Aerobic test
days.work: Complete the 1-mile run/walk and resting heart rate.

days.title: Muscular test
days.work: Complete push-up, curl-up, and plank tests.

days.title: Flexibility test
days.work: Complete sit-and-reach and shoulder stretch.

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Compare results across baseline, midyear, and final.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a fitness report.

weeks.topic: Five-year fitness plan and final reflection
objectives: Create a five-year plan for lifelong activity

days.title: Five-year plan
days.work: Write a 5-year fitness plan covering college or work life, with yearly goals for each fitness component.

days.title: Barriers
days.work: List likely barriers after high school (schedule, cost, location) and a specific strategy and community resource for each.

days.title: Lead a workout
days.work: Plan and lead a 40-minute family workout combining cardio, strength, and flexibility.

days.title: Presentation
days.work: Present your five-year plan and year-long fitness data in a 5-minute talk.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a 400-word reflection on how your attitudes toward fitness changed this year.
